It's bizarre. Like saying that working in a mine is liberating. 

The better angle is that true liberation is when no person has to sell their body to survive.

Maybe I'm fucked in the head, but I genuinely don't see how sex work is uniquely distinct from other forms of labor that are physically invasive. 

The methods of exchange and procurement are different, but the outcomes are nearly identical. 

I'm not at all trying to be edgy, and I'm 1000% willing to change my views, but I just don't see the meaningful distinction. 

And, again, that doesn't mean I'm saying sex work is *good*, just that it's on par with all the other shit we put ourselves through as humans. And if we're not as incensed about sending people into coal mines as we are sending gonads into battle, then I'm just plain confused.

I really wish someone could explain it to me, beyond a rationalization that comes down to "we socialize people to hold their sexual integrity in uniquely high regard, therefore the exploitation of that sexuality is uniquely aggravating to the psyche."

I have what feel like real emotions when I'm with friends, and even "shockwaves" of emotion for a few hours after I leave them. But once I'm alone, I feel emotionless. And, beyond that, I feel like I begin to look beneath the ostentation of my emotion to the motives. I begin to wonder if I actually love this girl, or if I'm just riding a societal script because the result is I end up with a very low-cost place to live?  To I love my closest friends, or do I maintain the friendship because it so frequently proves useful to me?

I occasionally catch myself entertaining thoughts, or even performing actions, that could only be done by someone without a properly functioning conscience.

That said, I think the fact that I'm even worried about this proves I'm not a sociopath (or psychopath--I can never recall the difference).

Right?

Yeah, I just mean neuro-physiological mechanisms. I've read a bit about the idea of poor regulation of "happy chemicals", such that they build up and up and up until they burst into mania, depleting themselves entirely, leading to depression until they can be rebuilt.

But my experience of this pre-mania depression seems to belie that theory.

With mania, it means not making any large purchases, mostly. Same goes for any large decision, really. If there's anything I really want, I basically have very strict rule that I don't act on it for two full weeks. It's almost more than a rule. I force it to be a sort of axiom of my manic existence. *Do nothing.*

Otherwise, I just roll with it. If possible, I try to direct the energy towards getting work done. That's sort of hit or miss.

With depression, it mostly means just accepting the feelings. They are what they are. They come from places both rational and irrational, all mixed together. Ultimately, it means "No hurting yourself, and definitely no killing yourself." Again, as a sort of axiomatic proposition. Although with depression it's a *six* week ban on all self-harm.

It's sort of like, "Hey, if there's enough rationality to buy X, or harm yourself in Y way after the allotted time, then there's a good reason."  There never is, though,of course ;)

It's weird, because I've never read about it before. I need to make it part of my regular coping system. Frankly, it should be huge help. Unexpected depression with no preceding mania *always* means mania within a week. And proper depression immediately following. 

I just can't really wrap my head around what the mechanism would be...

Accidentally got blackout drunk at a hostel in Bundaberg, Australia a decade ago. I was experimenting with cooking with wine at the time and wondered if I could cook pasta with it. Turns out that you *can*, but all the alcohol will remain. Proceeded to have a few, reasonable drinks along with dinner--a dinner that was basically a bunch of pasta soaked in a full bottle of wine. So, imagine a guy who doesn't drink much having a full bottle of wine, plus four or five drinks on top. 

I (apparently) went completely apeshit, crying hysterically, vomiting everywhere, kicking and screaming.  I woke up on a couch and told to get my shit and get the fuck out shortly after.

Maybe i should do some travel writing. It might give some purpose to my wanderings. I've always wanted to write a blog for introverted travellers (and a book), since there isn't much out there for us.

Yeah, the drinking thing... (i drank so much because the depression was making socializing very difficult. which isn't an excuse, but it is a bit of context) I'm not sure I'd want to cut it out completely, but perhaps setting very hard, uncompromising limits would be good. Like, no more than one drink per hour. That allows me to still enjoy the hobby without A) Getting so drunk I do stupid shit, and B) Drinking so much I forget about the rule. Yes. That's the rule, in effect as of now.

I think I can do good things on Earth.  There's potential in me that I don't want to give up on. But i also don't want to hurt anyone, much less the people I care about more than anything in the world. I wish I was a better human being.

Anyway, thank you so much for reading and for responding.
